AiProvenance.description:
Attached to every string a model wrote.

The UI renders its `✨ Generated by AI` pill from these fields. The frontend
is never asked to infer whether a title came from a model or an analyst --
that inference would be wrong exactly when it matters, on a narrative an
analyst renamed after disagreeing with the model.

edited_by_user.description: True once an analyst has edited the string. Reclustering must not overwrite it.
edited_by_user.title: Edited By User

generated_by.description: 'ai' = written by a language model. 'heuristic' = derived from centroid keywords with no model in the loop. 'human' = written or edited by an analyst.
generated_by.title: Generated By

model.description: Model id that produced the string.
model.title: Model

AiProvenance.title: AiProvenance

AlertCondition.description:
A single threshold. Deliberately not a query language.

An expression DSL here would be a small interpreter with an injection
surface, evaluated against the corpus on a beat schedule. One metric, one
operator, one value covers every rule the UI spec asks for.
AlertCondition.title: AlertCondition

payload.description: The metric value and the condition that fired, so the alert is self-explaining.
payload.title: Payload

cooldown_minutes.description: Minimum gap between two alerts from this rule for the same subject. Without it a narrative hovering on a threshold fires every evaluation cycle and the analyst stops reading alerts.
cooldown_minutes.title: Cooldown Minutes

ApiKeyCreated.description:
The mint response.

``key`` appears here and nowhere else, ever. It is not recoverable: only a
peppered hash is stored, and a lost key is reissued rather than looked up.

key.description: The plaintext key. Shown once. Store it now; it cannot be recovered.
key.title: Key

ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated

ApiKeyOut.description: A key as listed. Never contains the secret.
ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut

community_id.description: Louvain community over the co-posting graph.
community_id.title: Community Id

created_at_source.description: Account creation date at the platform, when exposed.
created_at_source.title: Created At Source

is_bot_flagged.description: The platform's own bot flag where one exists (Mastodon exposes it). Distinct from bot_score, which is this system's estimate.
is_bot_flagged.title: Is Bot Flagged

skip_reasons.description: Why a score is null. News/RSS 'authors' are outlets, not people, so account-level bot scoring is skipped there rather than fabricated.
skip_reasons.title: Skip Reasons

AuthorScoreExplanation.description:
Feature-level attribution for the bot score.

A bot probability with no explanation is the black-box number this product
exists to argue against, so the top contributing features travel with it.

caveat.description: Model limitations that bear on this specific score, e.g. weak generalisation to campaigns unlike the training set. Surfaced rather than buried in a report.
caveat.title: Caveat

components.description: The risk-score decomposition, when risk was computed.
components.title: Components

top_features.description: Highest-|contribution| account features, signed toward or against 'bot'.
top_features.title: Top Features

AuthorScoreExplanation.title: AuthorScoreExplanation

char_start.description: Start of the span in `context` this citation supports.
char_start.title: Char Start

snippet.description: The retrieved passage the claim was generated over.
snippet.title: Snippet

post_pct.description: Share of the project's posts written by this cohort.
post_pct.title: Post Pct

ComparisonMetricRow.description: One row of the UI's 'CW v. WM v. RS' table.

values.description: narrative_id -> value. Null where the metric was not measured for that narrative.
values.title: Values

ComparisonMetricRow.title: ComparisonMetricRow

caution_note.description: What the reader should not conclude from this context.
caution_note.title: Caution Note

context.description: A hedged analyst note over retrieved sources. Empty string when verification_status is insufficient_evidence -- an empty field is honest where an uncited paragraph is not.
context.title: Context

superseded_by.description: Set when a regeneration replaced this row. Never mutated.
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

CompassFeedback.description: Thumbs up/down, stored for the writeup's error analysis.
CompassFeedback.title: CompassFeedback

ConceptItem.description: An extracted topic or entity for the concept cloud.
ConceptItem.title: ConceptItem

domain.description: Registrable domain, lowercased. Subdomains roll up to it.
domain.title: Domain

enrichment_detail.description: Why enrichment is unavailable, when it is.
enrichment_detail.title: Enrichment Detail

link_velocity.description: Posts per hour carrying this domain at peak.
link_velocity.title: Link Velocity

sharing_author_bot_ratio.description: Share of the authors linking it that score bot-like.
sharing_author_bot_ratio.title: Sharing Author Bot Ratio

author_count.description: Distinct authors using it. Null for the author tab itself.
author_count.title: Author Count

label.description: Display name, e.g. a handle for an author.
label.title: Label

Engagement.description:
Four counters, every one of them nullable, and that is the whole point.

``null`` is not ``0``. Reddit exposes no view count, so ``views`` is null
there and a sum over a mixed corpus must skip it rather than adding zero --
otherwise "average views per post" silently halves the moment Reddit is
included in the filter.
Engagement.title: Engagement

GeneratedText.description: A string plus how it came to exist.
GeneratedText.title: GeneratedText

GraphBucket.description: One stop on the UI's time scrubber.
GraphBucket.title: GraphBucket

bucket_start.description: Which scrubber bucket this edge belongs to.
bucket_start.title: Bucket Start

colour_role.description: Semantic role, not a hex value. Theming belongs to the frontend.
colour_role.title: Colour Role

layout.description: Layout algorithm, or 'client' when small enough to lay out live.
layout.title: Layout

modularity.description: Louvain modularity of the community partition, when computed.
modularity.title: Modularity

truncation.description: {'applied_max_nodes', 'dropped_nodes', 'dropped_edges', 'min_degree_kept'}. A dropped periphery makes a cluster look more isolated than it is, so the response says exactly what was removed and by what rule.
truncation.title: Truncation

HighRiskPost.description: A row of the overview's high-risk posts panel.

force.description: Ignore Phase 1's per-source checkpoints and refetch the window. Expensive and quota-consuming; the default resumes.
force.title: Force

mode.description: 'fetch' runs the Phase 1 adapters to Parquet. 'load' bulk-copies existing Parquet into Postgres. 'both' chains them.

sources.description: Empty means every source with credentials configured.

rejects_path.description: Parquet file holding the rejected rows for inspection.
rejects_path.title: Rejects Path

JobAccepted.description:
The 202 body for anything that starts work.

One shape for every async operation, so the frontend polls one endpoint
regardless of what it kicked off.
JobAccepted.title: JobAccepted

detail.description: Cancellation is cooperative: a running task stops at its next checkpoint rather than being killed mid-write, so a cancelled job may report partial progress that is already durably committed.
detail.title: Detail

progress.description: Fraction complete. Monotonic within a run, but a resumed task starts from where it left off rather than at zero -- tasks are resumable, and resetting progress on a retry would make a resume look like a restart.
progress.title: Progress

KpiBundle.description:
The five headline KPIs, in the fixed order the UI renders them.

The order is part of the contract. The dashboard's top row is Posts,
Engagements, Authors, Sentiment, Emotions, and a response that reorders them
would silently reshuffle the page.

comparison_window.description: The preceding window that delta_pct compares against.
comparison_window.title: Comparison Window

KpiBundle.title: KpiBundle

confidence.description: Calibrated probability for the reported verdict, not the raw logit.
confidence.title: Confidence

explanation.description: Plain-language account of what the model saw and how much weight it deserves. Required on a completed check: a bare number is not an acceptable answer to this question.

limitations.description: Known failure modes bearing on this specific check -- compression, resolution, no face found, out-of-distribution generator.
limitations.title: Limitations

media_type.description: MIME type detected from magic bytes.
media_type.title: Media Type

retention.description: {'deletes_at', 'retention_hours'}. Uploaded media is imagery of real people and is purged on a timer; the API states when.
retention.title: Retention

Metric.description:
A KPI value that carries its own definition.

The UI spec requires a `(?)` tooltip on every KPI explaining exactly how it
was computed. That text is the backend's job, not the frontend's: only the
backend knows what the query actually summed, which nulls it skipped, and
which rows the filter excluded. A frontend-authored definition is a guess
that goes stale the first time the query changes.

delta_pct.description: Change against the preceding window of equal length, if computed.
delta_pct.title: Delta Pct

Metric.title: Metric

This is the product thesis in one response body. A number the UI cannot

The six fields the UI renders on every narrative surface.

``fusion_score`` is 0-100 and ``priority`` is derived from it by thresholds

same score can never carry different priorities.

info.description:
Narrative Intelligence Platform -- Phase 4 backend.

Detects, clusters and scores coordinated misinformation narratives across
platforms. Every score this API returns is decomposable: a `components` blob and
a `scoring_version` accompany every number, and every AI-generated string
carries `generated_by`, the model id and a generation timestamp.

**Conventions**

* Auth: `X-API-Key` header. Reads need the `read` scope, mutations `write`,
  key management `admin`.
* Lists are cursor-paginated: `?cursor=&limit=` (default 50, max 200).
* Anything expensive returns `202` with a `job_id`; poll `/api/v1/jobs/{id}`.
* Errors share one envelope: `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "request_id"}}`.
info.title: Narrative Intelligence Platform API
